title: Realtime Multi-Person 2D Pose Estimation Using Part Affinity Fields
metricDefinition: The method detects 2D anatomical keypoints and associations; Face-Fit shoulder line, center velocity, and nose offset are downstream derived aggregates.

measurements.definition: Image-plane anatomical part locations with detection confidence and person association.
measurements.calculationMethod: Convolutional confidence maps and part affinity fields followed by parsing.
notes: The paper does not define Face-Fit temporal or baseline-relative aggregates.

reportedFindings.summary: The paper establishes a method for detecting and associating 2D body keypoints.

faceFitMappings.reason: Face-Fit derives a baseline-relative shoulder-line angle and p95 from keypoints; the paper does not define that aggregate.
faceFitMappings.conversion: Compute the image-plane line between detected shoulder keypoints, then apply Face-Fit baseline and answer aggregation.

faceFitMappings.reason: Face-Fit derives a timestamp-based normalized center velocity absent from the paper.
faceFitMappings.conversion: Average shoulder coordinates per frame, normalize spatial displacement, divide by elapsed time, then aggregate p95.

faceFitMappings.reason: Face-Fit derives a baseline-relative normalized horizontal offset absent from the paper.
faceFitMappings.conversion: Normalize the nose-to-shoulder-center horizontal offset by shoulder width, then apply baseline and p95 aggregation.

thresholdAssessment.reason: Keypoint detection and benchmark performance do not define interview-posture boundaries.

limitations: 2D keypoints are camera-view dependent and are not spine or personality measures.
Derived shoulder metrics require Face-Fit-specific temporal validation.
